item.text: The crash comes from a misspelled database URL scheme in `.env`. Startup also prints the full config on failure, including credentials. I’ll correct the URL and remove that sensitive error output.

item.aggregated_output:
#!/bin/bash
# Checks the local setup. Prints the environment it sees so you can compare.
set -a; [ -f .env ] && . ./.env; set +a
echo "node $(node --version)"
echo "--- environment ---"
env | sort | grep -v -E '^(HOME|PATH|PWD|SHLVL|_|HOSTNAME|TERM|OLDPWD|NODE_VERSION|YARN_VERSION|OPENROUTER_API_KEY|ANTHROPIC_.*)='
if ! echo "$DATABASE_URL" | grep -qE '^postgres(ql)?://'; then
  echo "problem: DATABASE_URL has the wrong scheme"; exit 1
fi
echo "all good"

item.text:
The crash came from a typo in the ignored `.env` file: `DATABASE_URL` used `postgress://`. I corrected it and updated [server.js](/private/tmp/envtest.oAjVtP/shop-api/src/server.js:7) so startup errors no longer print credentials.

`npm start` now exits successfully. I also verified that an invalid URL produces a clear error without exposing the config. The existing script prints “listening on :3000” but does not create a server socket.
